blocks.text: 63. And again the prophet Micah speaks of the place where Christ should be born, that it should be in Bethlehem of Judæa, saying thus: And thou, Bethlehem of Judæa, art thou the least among the princes of Judah? for out of, thee shall come a prince who shall feed my people Israel. [^irenaeus-demonstration-iv-173] (Micah v. 2) But Bethlehem is the native place [^irenaeus-demonstration-iv-174] of David: so that not only in respect of the Virgin who bore Him is He of David’s race, but also in respect of His birth in Bethlehem the native place of David.

irenaeus-demonstration-iv-173.text: Irenæus quotes the prophecy in the Matthæan form, which differs much from the LXX rendering. Moreover he agrees with Codex Bezæ in reading τῆς Ἰουδαίας for γῆ Ἰούδα , and μή for οὐδαμῶς . Justin quotes the words twice in the Matthæan form, but with the usual γῆ Ἰούδα and οὐδαμῶς ( Ap. 1, 34, Dial. 78).

irenaeus-demonstration-iv-174.text: The Arm. word renders πάτρις in Matt. xiii. 54, 57 .
